intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Join a guided game drive to observe predator-prey interactions, big cats, and diverse wildlife in their natural habitat across the vast savannah plains.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the iconic backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Take a guided safari drive to observe elephants, lions, cheetahs, and over 400 bird species while enjoying breathtaking panoramic views of Africa's highest peak.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Participate in a guided bush walk with armed rangers to track rhinos on foot, learn about conservation efforts, and encounter chimpanzees at the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary within the conservancy.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Discover the stunning alkaline Lake Nakuru, famous for its millions of pink flamingos that paint the shoreline in vivid color. Explore the surrounding national park to spot white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, leopards, and over 450 bird species in a compact but incredibly diverse ecosystem.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Samburu National Reserve Rare Species Game Drive
experiences.description: Venture into the remote and rugged Samburu National Reserve to discover Kenya's 'Samburu Special Five' — the Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx — species found nowhere else in Kenya. Experience authentic bush culture with visits to traditional Samburu warrior villages and sundowner game drives along the Ewaso Ng'iro River.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or matatu shared taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a 24-hour convenience store near the resort upon arrival - budget around KES 500-800

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book an airport shuttle in advance to save money. Avoid unmarked taxis at the airport. Keep KES 2,000-3,000 in cash handy for transport and tips on arrival night.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a relaxed walk along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings. Explore the local area on foot and visit a nearby local market to exchange currency at a bureau de change for the best rates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest town center for orientation. Browse local craft stalls and pick up a budget SIM card (Safaricom recommended) for data and local calls. Stroll along the beach and enjoy the warm 25°C weather. Rent a bicycle (approx KES 500/hour) to explore the coastal area.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beachfront. Head to a local open-air restaurant or 'nyama choma' spot near the resort for an authentic Kenyan dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local tea house - mandazi (fried dough) and chai tea, budget KES 200-400
meals.lunch: Local beach snack stall - grilled corn, samosas, or chapati with beans, budget KES 300-500
meals.dinner: Local nyama choma restaurant - grilled goat or chicken with ugali and sukuma wiki, budget KES 600-900

day_by_day.notes: July is warm and dry - perfect beach weather at 25°C with only 30mm rain expected this month. Carry sunscreen and stay hydrated. Get a Safaricom data SIM for affordable internet access throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk along the coastal forest or mangrove area near the resort. Kenya's coast is rich with over 200 bird species. Bring binoculars if available or rent from a local guide (KES 300-500). Look for kingfishers, herons, and sunbirds in the mangroves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local nature reserve or marine park nearby. Snorkeling at a budget-friendly reef spot (KES 1,500-2,500 including basic gear rental). The warm July waters offer excellent visibility for reef fish, sea turtles, and colorful corals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Relax on the beach and enjoy the evening breeze. Visit a local beachside bar for a cold Tusker beer (KES 200-300) and watch local fishermen bring in their catch.

meals.breakfast: Local guesthouse breakfast - eggs, bread, and chai, budget KES 300-500
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beach shack - grilled fish with coconut rice, budget KES 500-800
meals.dinner: Self-catering or resort restaurant - buy fresh fish from local fishermen (KES 300-500) and cook at resort if facilities available, or dine at a local Swahili restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate snorkeling prices in advance and go with a licensed operator. Avoid touching coral reefs to protect the marine ecosystem. July is peak season so book activities a day ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Full day trip to Shimba Hills National Reserve (if near Diani/South Coast) or Arabuko-Sokoke Forest Reserve (if near Malindi/Watamu). Take an early morning matatu or shared taxi (KES 200-400 each way). These reserves offer elephant sightings, leopards, and rare Sokoke scops owl at very affordable entry fees (KES 215 for residents, ~USD 25 for non-residents).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue wildlife game walk inside the reserve with a budget KWS ranger guide (KES 500-1,000). Look for elephants, buffalo, sable antelope, and diverse bird species. The dry July weather means animals congregate around water sources making sightings easier.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by matatu. Rest and freshen up. Stroll to a local market for fresh tropical fruits - mangoes, pineapples, and passion fruit are in season and very cheap (KES 50-100 each).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at resort - bread, peanut butter, and fruit, budget KES 200-400
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local bakery before departing - samosas, mandazi, and bottled water, budget KES 400-600
meals.dinner: Local Swahili restaurant near resort - pilau rice with chicken or fish curry, budget KES 600-900

day_by_day.notes: Start early (by 7:00am) to maximize wildlife sightings in the cooler morning hours. Wear neutral earth-tone clothing for game walks. Carry at least 2 liters of water per person. Book a shared group tour to split guide costs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local Swahili village or cultural center near the resort for a guided cultural walk (KES 500-1,000). Learn about traditional Swahili architecture, dhow boat building, and coastal Kenyan culture. Many villages near the coast offer authentic low-cost cultural experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby historical site - visit ruins such as Gede Ruins (near Watamu) or Fort Jesus (Mombasa) depending on location. Entry fees are affordable (KES 200-500 for residents, USD 5-15 for non-residents). These UNESCO-linked sites offer fascinating history of the Swahili coast.
day_by_day.evening: Evening dhow sunset cruise - many operators offer budget group dhow rides along the coast at sunset (KES 1,500-2,500 per person including light snacks). A quintessential Kenyan coastal experience.

meals.breakfast: Local tea house - mandazi, mahamri (coconut doughnuts), and spiced chai, budget KES 200-350
meals.lunch: Street food near historical site - mishkaki (grilled meat skewers), samosas, and fresh juice, budget KES 400-600
meals.dinner: Beachfront local restaurant - fresh grilled lobster or prawns (seasonal budget catch) with chips or rice, budget KES 800-1,200

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting Swahili villages and historical sites out of cultural respect. Bargain respectfully at craft markets - initial prices are often 2-3x the fair price. Dhow cruise bookings are best made the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tsavo East or Tsavo West National Park - Kenya's largest national park system. Book a budget group safari day trip in advance (KES 8,000-15,000 per person including transport, park fees, and a basic lunch). Depart by 6:00am for best wildlife viewing. Look for elephants, lions, leopards, cheetahs, and the famous red elephants of Tsavo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue game drive inside Tsavo. Visit Mzima Springs in Tsavo West - a crystal-clear oasis where hippos and crocodiles can be observed from an underwater viewing chamber. Spot giraffes, zebras, and wildebeest on the open savannah plains.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by early evening (approximately 18:00-19:00). Tired but exhilarated - rest and relax at the resort. Share safari stories and photos over dinner.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast at resort before departure - fruit, bread, and tea, budget KES 200-300
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included in safari tour or basic lodge lunch stop - sandwiches and juice, included in tour cost
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or local eatery - treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal to celebrate the safari day, budget KES 800-1,200

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight wildlife day of the trip. Book through a reputable budget operator - compare at least 3 quotes. Tsavo is best in July as dry season concentrates animals near rivers. Bring a camera with zoom lens, binoculars, and dust protection for your gear. Park fees are included in most group tour packages.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the Tsavo safari. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a swim at the resort beach. Take a morning yoga session on the beach or a gentle walk along the shoreline collecting shells. The warm 25°C July morning is perfect for this.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local turtle conservation project or marine wildlife sanctuary (many operate along the Kenyan coast near Watamu, Diani, and Malindi - entry KES 500-1,000). Learn about sea turtle nesting, rehabilitation of injured marine animals, and coral reef restoration efforts. A wonderful budget-friendly nature and conservation experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local beach bonfire or cultural performance if available near the resort. Many beach resorts and local communities organize evening cultural shows with traditional Giriama or Swahili dancing (KES 500-1,000 or sometimes free).

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast or local café - eggs, toast, tropical fruit, and fresh juice, budget KES 400-600
meals.lunch: Beach picnic - buy fresh fruits, bread, cheese, and local snacks from a nearby supermarket, budget KES 500-700
meals.dinner: Local Kenyan restaurant - githeri (corn and bean stew) or mukimo (mashed potatoes with greens) for an authentic upcountry Kenyan meal, budget KES 400-700

day_by_day.notes: Turtle conservation projects often allow volunteers to assist with evening nest monitoring for a small donation. This is a memorable low-cost wildlife experience. Check with the resort reception for recommended local conservation projects.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding along the calm coastal waters (rental KES 500-1,000/hour). Explore mangrove channels by kayak - a peaceful way to spot wildlife including monitor lizards, crabs, and wading birds in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fish market in the nearest town for a vibrant cultural experience. Watch fishermen auction fresh catches, interact with local vendors, and buy affordable fresh fish or seafood. Then visit a nearby spice garden or coconut plantation for a guided tour (KES 300-600) - learn about coastal Kenyan agriculture.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple Swahili meal using fresh market ingredients at the resort (if self-catering facilities available) or take a budget cooking class at a local community kitchen (KES 1,500-2,500) and learn to make coconut fish curry, chapati, and kachumbari salad.

meals.breakfast: Local tea house or resort - uji (fermented porridge) or oatmeal with honey and fruit, budget KES 200-400
meals.lunch: Fish market fresh catch - ask a vendor to grill your purchase on-site for a small fee, budget KES 400-700
meals.dinner: Self-cooked Swahili meal or cooking class meal - coconut fish curry with rice and fresh mango dessert, budget KES 500-800

day_by_day.notes: Mangrove kayaking is best done at high tide - check local tide charts the night before. The fish market is most active between 6:00-10:00am. Bargaining is expected and accepted at the fish market.

day_by_day.morning: Second safari experience - book a budget group day trip to a different wildlife area such as Amboseli National Park (famous for elephants with Mount Kilimanjaro backdrop) or Tsavo East's Lugard Falls. Depart early at 6:00am. Group shared safari costs approximately KES 8,000-14,000 per person all-inclusive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue game drive - Amboseli is renowned for the largest elephant herds in East Africa, Maasai giraffes, and spectacular views of Kilimanjaro on clear days. Visit the Observation Hill viewpoint for panoramic views over the park's swamps and plains.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by 19:00. Final evening beach walk under the stars. The July sky along the Kenyan coast offers spectacular stargazing with minimal light pollution away from town centers.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast before departure - fruit and energy bars, budget KES 200-300
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included in safari package or stop at a budget safari lodge for a set lunch, included in tour cost
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant - treat yourself to a full Swahili seafood feast, budget KES 1,000-1,500

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is approximately 5-6 hours from the coast so this is a very long day - start as early as possible. Alternatively, consider a closer half-day game drive at a local conservancy for a more relaxed final safari day. Confirm tour booking 2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning - wake up for a last sunrise beach walk and swim in the warm Indian Ocean. Pack souvenirs and gifts purchased throughout the trip. Visit a final local craft market for any last-minute shopping - Kenyan wood carvings, kikoi fabric, beaded jewelry, and Maasai crafts make excellent budget souvenirs (KES 200-2,000 depending on item).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final lunch at a local restaurant. Arrange airport transfer via matatu or pre-booked shuttle to Mombasa Moi International Airport or Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Kenya with incredible memories of wildlife, nature, and coastal beauty. Final airport meal or snacks while waiting for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or local café - enjoy a full Kenyan breakfast spread one last time, budget KES 400-700
meals.lunch: Last local meal - biryani rice with chicken or beef at a coastal Swahili restaurant, budget KES 600-900
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or food court - budget KES 800-1,500 depending on airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Keep some KES cash for airport departure taxes or last-minute expenses. Declare any wildlife products at customs - purchasing ivory or protected species products is illegal and heavily penalized. Total estimated budget for 10 days excluding flights: KES 45,000-70,000 (approximately USD 350-550) covering accommodation, food, activities, and local transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Kenya Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Join a guided game drive to observe predator-prey interactions, big cats, and diverse wildlife in their natural habitat across the vast savannah plains.

experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.description: Venture into the remote and rugged Samburu National Reserve to discover Kenya's 'Samburu Special Five' — the Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx — species found nowhere else in Kenya. Experience authentic bush culture with visits to traditional Samburu warrior villages and sundowner game drives along the Ewaso Ng'iro River.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle into Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged resort transfer. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and unwind with a welcome drink at the lobby bar before retiring for the night.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack or room service at Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival (mid-range room service menu)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your airport transfer with Aegean Bliss Resort in advance. Keep a small carry-on with essentials (change of clothes, toiletries) for easy access after the long flight. Currency exchange or M-Pesa SIM card can be arranged at the airport arrivals hall.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a relaxed orientation walk along the beachfront to get your bearings, breathe in the coastal air, and shake off any jet lag. Explore the resort grounds and nearby beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided half-day nature and coastal ecology walk organized through the resort. Discover local coastal flora, birdlife, and marine ecosystems along the Kenyan coastline. Look out for kingfishers, herons, and coastal raptors common in warm July weather.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's beachfront terrace. Enjoy the warm 25°C evening breeze off the Indian Ocean. Early dinner and an early bedtime to recover from travel and prepare for the safari adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort's main restaurant — included or available at mid-range supplement
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch at the resort's poolside grill — grilled fish, fresh salads, and tropical fruit (budget ~$15–20 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's main dining room — try Swahili coastal cuisine such as coconut fish curry, pilau rice, and kachumbari salad (budget ~$25–35 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day as a gentle acclimatization day. July is warm and dry — perfect beach weather. Apply sunscreen generously. Visit the resort's tour desk to confirm all upcoming safari bookings and transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure by road or light aircraft transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 4–5 hours by road from Nairobi, or arrange a connecting flight). Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari with a certified guide. Witness the breathtaking spectacle of millions of pink flamingos painting the alkaline lake shores pink in the crisp morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Lake Nakuru game drive through the park's acacia and euphorbia forests. Spot white and black rhinos, Rothschild's giraffes, lions, leopards, and over 400 bird species. The warm July weather provides excellent visibility and comfortable game-viewing conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your mid-range lodge near Lake Nakuru (e.g., Sarova Lion Hill Game Lodge or similar). Freshen up and enjoy sundowners on the lodge veranda overlooking the Rift Valley escarpment. Debrief the day's sightings with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or quick breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch enjoyed at a designated picnic site inside Lake Nakuru National Park — arranged by your guide
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge restaurant — hearty Kenyan buffet with nyama choma (roasted meat), ugali, sukuma wiki, and local stews (budget ~$30–40 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Flamingo numbers fluctuate — July typically offers good sightings. Bring binoculars and a zoom lens camera. Park entry fees apply (~$60 USD per person for non-residents). Book the safari through a reputable mid-range operator for a shared game drive vehicle to keep costs manageable.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn game drive at Lake Nakuru National Park — early morning is the best time to spot predators and rhinos in active behavior. Look for leopards resting in fig trees and lions patrolling the lake's southern shores. Return to the lodge for a full breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Lake Nakuru and transfer to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approximately 3 hours north via Nakuru–Nyahururu–Nanyuki road). Check in to your mid-range accommodation at Ol Pejeta (e.g., Sweetwaters Serena Camp or similar tented camp). Afternoon Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking experience — visit the Baraka Rhino Sanctuary to meet the last two northern white rhinos in the world (Najin and Fatu) and track critically endangered black rhinos with expert rangers.
day_by_day.evening: Chimpanzee sanctuary evening visit (unique to Ol Pejeta — the only place in Kenya to see chimpanzees). Sundowner drinks in the bush. Return to camp for dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch en route at a local mid-range restaurant in Nyahururu town — try githeri (maize and beans) or a hearty meat stew with chapati (budget ~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ol Pejeta camp restaurant — bush-style BBQ with game meat options, salads, and dessert (budget ~$35–45 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta Conservancy charges a conservation fee (~$90 USD per person per day for non-residents — includes game drives). The northern white rhinos are a once-in-a-lifetime encounter; be respectful and follow ranger instructions. Bring a warm layer for evening as temperatures drop at the higher Laikipia altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Ol Pejeta Conservancy game drive starting at sunrise. The conservancy is home to the Big Five — lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, and buffaloes. July's dry season means animals congregate around water sources, making for spectacular wildlife viewing. Visit the Dan Foster Memorial and learn about conservation efforts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive focusing on the conservancy's lion prides and large elephant herds. Stop at the Ewaso Nyiro River for hippo and crocodile viewing. Photography enthusiasts will love the golden afternoon light on Mount Kenya's distant snow-capped peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner stop at a scenic bush lookout point. Return to camp for a relaxed evening. Optional cultural visit to a nearby Maasai or Samburu community village (arranged through the camp, ~$15–20 USD per person).

meals.breakfast: Full bush breakfast at Ol Pejeta camp
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch in the bush — enjoyed at a scenic picnic spot inside the conservancy
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at camp — roasted vegetables, slow-cooked beef or chicken stew, and fresh fruit crumble for dessert (included in lodge package or ~$40 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta is malaria-risk area — take prescribed anti-malarials and use DEET-based insect repellent. The conservancy is one of Kenya's best for rhino conservation storytelling — engage with the rangers and learn about anti-poaching efforts. Weather in July is dry and clear — ideal game-viewing conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Ol Pejeta Conservancy and transfer south to Amboseli National Park (approximately 5–6 hours via Nairobi, or arrange a light aircraft charter from Nanyuki airstrip for a more comfortable and scenic 1.5-hour flight). Arrive at your mid-range Amboseli lodge (e.g., Amboseli Sopa Lodge or Kibo Safari Camp) and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views experience with an afternoon game drive. Amboseli is world-famous for its massive elephant herds with Mount Kilimanjaro (Africa's highest peak) as a dramatic backdrop. July's clear skies offer the best chances of seeing Kilimanjaro without cloud cover. Observe matriarch-led elephant families at close range.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a designated viewpoint with Kilimanjaro silhouetted against the orange and pink sunset sky — one of Africa's most iconic views. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Ol Pejeta camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Amboseli lodge upon arrival — buffet-style with salads, grilled meats, and Kenyan dishes (budget ~$20–25 USD or included in half-board package)
meals.dinner: Dinner at lodge restaurant — Amboseli-style buffet featuring local Maasai-inspired dishes, grilled meats, and vegetarian options (budget ~$35–45 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli National Park entry fees apply (~$60 USD per person). Mount Kilimanjaro is best visible in the early morning before clouds build — wake up early for sunrise photography. Amboseli's swamps are fed by underground streams from Kilimanjaro's glaciers, supporting remarkable biodiversity year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a sunrise game drive in Amboseli — this is the golden hour for elephant photography with Kilimanjaro glowing in the morning light. Visit the famous Observation Hill for panoramic views over the park's swamps and plains. Spot large elephant bulls, hippos, cape buffaloes, lions, cheetahs, and hundreds of bird species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Maasai village (Enkiama or similar) for a cultural immersion experience — watch traditional dances, learn about Maasai beadwork, and gain insight into how indigenous communities coexist with wildlife (~$20–30 USD per person). Return to the lodge for a late lunch and afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the lodge. Optional guided night walk around the lodge perimeter with a Maasai ranger — spot nocturnal wildlife including genets, civets, and bush babies. Stargazing session in Amboseli's dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Packed early morning coffee and snacks for the sunrise game drive; full breakfast upon return to lodge
meals.lunch: Late lunch at the lodge — light sandwiches, soup, and fresh juice (budget ~$15–20 USD)
meals.dinner: Special Maasai-themed dinner at the lodge with traditional storytelling by Maasai warriors — nyama choma, roasted maize, and honey-based desserts (budget ~$35–45 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Respect Maasai cultural protocols during the village visit — ask permission before photographing individuals. Amboseli's dust can be intense — bring a buff or scarf to cover your nose during game drives. The park's elephant population is one of the most studied in the world; your guides can share fascinating behavioral insights.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Amboseli — transfer by road or light aircraft to the Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 1-hour flight from Amboseli airstrip). Check in to your mid-range Mara camp (e.g., Mara Sopa Lodge, Keekorok Lodge, or a reputable mid-range tented camp). The Maasai Mara is the crown jewel of Kenyan safari.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari game drive — July is peak Great Migration season! Millions of wildebeest, zebras, and Thomson's gazelles are actively moving through the Mara ecosystem. Witness massive herds stretching to the horizon on the golden Mara plains. Spot the Big Five alongside the migration spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks in the Mara bush — watch the wildebeest herds settle for the evening as lion prides begin to stir. Return to camp for a celebratory dinner marking the halfway point of your safari adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Amboseli lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mara camp upon arrival — buffet with Kenyan and international options (included in most lodge packages or ~$25 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Mara lodge — bush BBQ under the stars with live Maasai cultural performance (budget ~$40–50 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Maasai Mara National Reserve fees apply (~$80 USD per person per day for non-residents). July–August is THE peak time for the Great Migration — book your camp well in advance as this is the most sought-after safari experience in Africa. The Mara River crossing (wildebeest vs. crocodiles) can be witnessed from late July onward — ask your guide for the latest crossing updates.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — depart at dawn for the best game viewing. Position yourselves near the Mara River for the possibility of witnessing a wildebeest river crossing — one of nature's most dramatic wildlife events. Crocodiles lurk in the murky waters as thousands of wildebeest gather courage to cross. Predator action is intense during migration season — lions, cheetahs, and leopards all capitalize on the abundance of prey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Mara's vast plains. Visit the Mara Triangle (managed by the Mara Conservancy) for less crowded game viewing. Spot large cheetah coalitions, serval cats, and enormous elephant herds. Hot air balloon safari option available for an additional cost (~$450–500 USD per person) — book in advance for a dawn balloon flight over the migration.
day_by_day.evening: Bush sundowner with your guide at a scenic Mara viewpoint. Return to camp for a special farewell bush dinner — tables set under acacia trees with lantern lighting, celebrating the end of your main safari circuit.

meals.breakfast: Packed bush breakfast eaten in the field near the Mara River at sunrise — a magical experience
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the Mara Triangle — arranged by your guide with fresh sandwiches, fruit, and drinks
meals.dinner: Special outdoor bush dinner at camp — three-course meal with wine pairing, candlelit under the African sky (budget ~$45–55 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Mara River crossing is never guaranteed on any specific day — be patient and trust your guide's experience. Avoid overcrowding at crossing sites by choosing a responsible operator who maintains distance. Bring a high-capacity memory card and extra camera batteries — you will take hundreds of photos. Tipping your guide (suggested ~$15–20 USD per day) is customary and greatly appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in the Maasai Mara — a leisurely last look at the migration herds and the Mara's iconic landscapes. Return to camp for a full breakfast and pack up. Depart the Mara by road or light aircraft back to Nairobi (approximately 5 hours by road or 45-minute flight). If time permits, stop at a Nairobi curio market (e.g., Maasai Market or Utamaduni Craft Centre) for authentic Kenyan souvenirs — Maasai beadwork, soapstone carvings, and batik fabrics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer back to the coast and return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Spend the final afternoon relaxing on the beachfront — swim in the Indian Ocean, enjoy a spa treatment, or simply soak in the warm 25°C sunshine and reflect on an extraordinary 10-day Kenyan adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant. Toast to an unforgettable Kenya trip with a glass of Kenyan wine or a Dawa cocktail (Kenya's famous vodka, honey, and lime cocktail). Pack and prepare for onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Mara camp before final departure
meals.lunch: Lunch en route — stop at a mid-range restaurant in Nairobi's Karen suburb (e.g., Talisman Restaurant or Carnivore for the classic Kenyan experience, budget ~$20–30 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh Swahili seafood feast with grilled lobster, prawns, and octopus in coconut sauce, with a slice of Kenyan mandazi for dessert (budget ~$40–55 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and arrange an airport transfer from Aegean Bliss Resort well in advance. Kenya's wildlife parks require a minimum of 2 days each to do justice — this itinerary has been optimized to give you a taste of Kenya's greatest highlights within 10 days. Keep a digital and physical copy of all park entry receipts and accommodation vouchers throughout your trip. A yellow fever vaccination certificate may be required for re-entry into certain countries — check requirements for your home country.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Join a guided game drive to observe predator-prey interactions, big cats, and diverse wildlife in their natural habitat across the vast savannah plains.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the iconic backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Take a guided safari drive to observe elephants, lions, cheetahs, and over 400 bird species while enjoying breathtaking panoramic views of Africa's highest peak.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Visit the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa and home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. Participate in a guided bush walk with armed rangers to track rhinos on foot, learn about conservation efforts, and encounter chimpanzees at the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary within the conservancy.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Discover the stunning alkaline Lake Nakuru, famous for its millions of pink flamingos that paint the shoreline in vivid color. Explore the surrounding national park to spot white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, leopards, and over 450 bird species in a compact but incredibly diverse ecosystem.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Samburu National Reserve Rare Species Game Drive
experiences.description: Venture into the remote and rugged Samburu National Reserve to discover Kenya's 'Samburu Special Five' — the Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx — species found nowhere else in Kenya. Experience authentic bush culture with visits to traditional Samburu warrior villages and sundowner game drives along the Ewaso Ng'iro River.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Welcome drink and late-night light supper upon check-in. Resort concierge briefing on the upcoming itinerary.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: On board flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome supper at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated cheese board, smoked salmon blinis, and a glass of champagne upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Private chauffeur with name board will meet you at arrivals. Luggage handling fully managed by resort staff. Ensure passport and travel documents are readily accessible for immigration. Resort check-in is available 24 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start after overnight arrival. Enjoy a lavish à la carte breakfast on the beachfront terrace of Aegean Bliss Resort overlooking the Indian Ocean. Orientation walk of the resort grounds with a personal concierge to familiarise yourself with all luxury amenities including the infinity pool, spa, and private beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure on the resort's private beach. Enjoy complimentary non-motorised water sports including kayaking and paddleboarding. Optional 90-minute welcome spa treatment at the resort's luxury spa — choose from a Swahili coastal massage or deep tissue therapy to recover from travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's clifftop bar with panoramic Indian Ocean views. Enjoy a premium sundowner experience with a curated cocktail menu and Kenyan canape selection featuring local flavours.

meals.breakfast: Lavish à la carte breakfast at the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, smoked fish, artisan pastries, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort beach club — grilled lobster salad, Swahili-spiced calamari, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — five-course tasting menu featuring Kenyan coastal cuisine including grilled prawns, mango ceviche, and Swahili-spiced rack of lamb, paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: This day is intentionally relaxed to allow recovery from long-haul travel. Spa bookings should be confirmed with the concierge upon arrival the previous evening. Dress code for the signature restaurant is smart casual.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from the nearest airstrip to the Maasai Mara National Reserve (approximately 1-hour scenic flight). Check in to a luxury tented camp within the Mara ecosystem. After settling in, embark on your first premium game drive in the Maasai Mara — the peak of the Great Migration season. Witness vast herds of wildebeest and zebras moving across the golden savannah with expert Maasai guides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration Safari experience with a dedicated afternoon game drive. Position your private vehicle at key river crossing points along the Mara River to witness the dramatic and thrilling wildebeest river crossings — one of nature's greatest spectacles. Accompanied by a private naturalist guide and a Maasai tracker.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks in the bush at a scenic viewpoint — champagne and canapés served on a private kopje or riverbank. Return to the luxury tented camp for a bush dinner under the stars around a traditional campfire, serenaded by the sounds of the African night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before charter flight — continental spread with fresh fruits, yoghurts, and hot items
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush picnic lunch served in the Maasai Mara — artisan sandwiches, cold meats, local cheeses, seasonal salads, and chilled beverages presented on linen-covered tables in a scenic bush setting
meals.dinner: Candlelit bush dinner at the luxury tented camp — three-course meal featuring slow-braised game stew, grilled fillet, and Kenyan coffee panna cotta, with fine South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Charter flight timings will be confirmed by the concierge. Pack light for the charter — soft-sided bags only (max 15kg). Neutral-coloured clothing recommended for game drives. Binoculars provided at camp. July is peak Great Migration season — river crossings are highly likely but not guaranteed as they depend on wildebeest movement.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for an exclusive hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise — one of Africa's most iconic luxury experiences. Float silently above the vast plains watching the Great Migration herds below, with Kilimanjaro visible on clear mornings. The flight lasts approximately one hour and is followed by a traditional champagne bush breakfast in the savannah.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp for a mid-morning rest. After lunch, enjoy a guided walking safari with an armed Maasai ranger — experience the Mara ecosystem at ground level, learning about tracks, plants, insects, and smaller wildlife often missed on game drives. Visit a traditional Maasai village (manyatta) for an authentic cultural interaction, including traditional dance, beadwork demonstrations, and a tour of the village.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner experience set up in the bush under a canopy of stars — a personal chef prepares a five-course meal at a beautifully decorated table in the wilderness. Accompanied by a sommelier with a premium wine pairing selection.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast following the hot air balloon safari — full English spread with smoked salmon, eggs cooked to order, fresh pastries, and sparkling wine served on linen tables in the open savannah
meals.lunch: Leisurely lunch at the luxury tented camp — grilled tilapia, Kenyan nyama choma (roasted meat), fresh salads, and tropical fruit platters
meals.dinner: Private five-course bush dinner under the stars — amuse-bouche, seared duck breast, Kenyan game consommé, herb-crusted lamb loin, and dark chocolate fondant with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon safari must be pre-booked well in advance — your concierge will have arranged this. Balloon flights are weather-dependent. Passengers must weigh under 100kg per balloon operator requirements. Walking safari requires closed-toe shoes. Maasai village visit includes a small community contribution fee which supports local livelihoods.

day_by_day.morning: Final early morning game drive in the Maasai Mara at golden hour — the best time to spot predators including lion, leopard, and cheetah. Your private guide will focus on tracking the Big Five and capturing the best photographic opportunities in the beautiful morning light. Return to camp for a full breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Maasai Mara to Amboseli National Park airstrip (approximately 1.5-hour scenic flight). Check in to a luxury lodge with iconic views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching experience with an afternoon game drive focused on Amboseli's legendary large elephant herds — some of Africa's most studied and photographed elephants — framed against the majestic snow-capped peak of Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive through Amboseli's open plains and swamp areas. Watch elephants gather at the water's edge as the sun sets behind Kilimanjaro — one of Africa's most photographed scenes. Return to the lodge for a welcome dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the Maasai Mara luxury camp — eggs, bacon, sausages, grilled tomatoes, fresh juice, and Kenyan tea and coffee
meals.lunch: In-flight snack pack provided during charter transfer; light lunch upon arrival at Amboseli lodge — mezze-style spread with local dips, flatbreads, and cold cuts
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the Amboseli luxury lodge — three-course meal with Kenyan-inspired dishes including avocado and prawn starter, slow-roasted beef tenderloin with local vegetables, and passion fruit tart

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli offers the best Kilimanjaro views in the morning before clouds build — ensure your camera is ready for dawn. July weather is generally clear and excellent for Kilimanjaro visibility. Soft bags only for charter flights. Amboseli is particularly famous for its large bull elephants with impressive tusks.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-sunrise game drive in Amboseli for the iconic Kilimanjaro and elephant photograph — the mountain is clearest at dawn before cloud cover develops. Visit the Observation Hill for panoramic views across the park's swamps, plains, and elephant herds below. Your private guide and wildlife photographer mentor will assist with camera settings and composition for world-class wildlife photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli Research Centre and learn about the long-term elephant research programme — one of the longest-running wildlife studies in the world. Interact with researchers and gain deep insight into elephant behaviour, family structures, and conservation challenges. Afternoon at leisure at the lodge — enjoy the infinity pool overlooking the Kilimanjaro panorama or relax with a spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner on a raised platform or in a scenic spot within the lodge grounds with unobstructed Kilimanjaro views. The lodge chef prepares a personalised menu. Stargazing session with a resident astronomer after dinner — the dark skies of Amboseli offer extraordinary celestial views.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast box for the pre-dawn game drive — freshly baked muffins, fruit, yoghurt, and a thermos of Kenyan coffee; full breakfast available upon return to lodge
meals.lunch: Gourmet poolside lunch at the lodge — grilled Nile perch, Kenyan chapati wraps with spiced chicken, and a selection of fresh salads with homemade dressings
meals.dinner: Private platform dinner — four-course meal including Kenyan crab bisque, grilled impala loin, truffle potato gratin, and a Kenyan honey and cardamom dessert, with premium wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Photography guide service should be confirmed with the lodge in advance. The Amboseli Research Centre visit is typically arranged through the lodge — a small donation to the research fund is appreciated. Evenings can be cool at altitude — bring a light layer for the stargazing session.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Amboseli to Ol Pejeta Conservancy (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check in to the luxury lodge within the conservancy. Begin the Ol Pejeta Rhino Tracking experience immediately — accompanied by expert rangers and trackers, venture on foot and by vehicle to locate and observe black rhinos in their natural habitat. Visit the dedicated sanctuary for the last two northern white rhinos on Earth — Sudan's daughters Najin and Fatu — a deeply moving conservation encounter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive within Ol Pejeta Conservancy — home to all of the Big Five. Visit the chimpanzee sanctuary, home to rescued chimpanzees from across Central Africa, and learn about their rehabilitation. Continue tracking wildlife including lions, leopards, and the remarkable density of black rhinos for which Ol Pejeta is famous.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner experience at a scenic conservancy viewpoint. Return to the lodge for dinner accompanied by a presentation from an Ol Pejeta conservancy ranger about rhino conservation efforts and the northern white rhino programme.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Amboseli lodge before charter transfer — full cooked breakfast with continental options
meals.lunch: Bush lunch served in the conservancy during the rhino tracking experience — gourmet picnic with artisan sandwiches, cold meats, local cheeses, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Ol Pejeta luxury lodge — three-course conservation-themed menu celebrating Kenyan produce: wild mushroom risotto, grilled grass-fed beef fillet from the conservancy's own cattle programme, and a dark chocolate and coffee mousse

day_by_day.notes: The northern white rhino encounter is an extraordinarily rare privilege — only two remain on Earth. Photography is permitted but respectful distance must be maintained. The Ol Pejeta Conservancy charges a conservation fee which directly funds rhino protection. Rhino tracking on foot requires a moderate level of fitness. Closed-toe shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Ol Pejeta focusing on predator activity — lions and leopards are most active at dawn. The conservancy's open plains and riverine forests offer excellent big cat sightings. Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary for a morning feeding session — an extraordinary experience watching these intelligent primates up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Ol Pejeta to Lake Nakuru (approximately 45 minutes). Check in to a luxury lodge on the lake's rim with panoramic views. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Bird Safari — the alkaline lake is famous for its millions of pink flamingos that create a breathtaking pink shoreline. Accompanied by an expert ornithologist guide, explore the lake's shores by vehicle, observing not only flamingos but also pelicans, African fish eagles, and over 450 recorded bird species.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the lake's edge watching the flamingo flocks take flight in spectacular pink clouds across the water — one of Africa's most visually stunning natural spectacles. Return to the lodge for dinner with views over the lake.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Ol Pejeta lodge — continental and cooked options, with a packed snack for the morning game drive
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Lake Nakuru lodge upon arrival — Kenyan-style buffet with fresh salads, grilled fish, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the Lake Nakuru luxury lodge — four-course dinner with lake views: smoked trout pâté, flamingo-pink beetroot and goat cheese salad, pan-seared Nile perch with lemon caper butter, and a mango and passion fruit pavlova, with curated East African wines

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers vary seasonally based on algae levels — July typically offers excellent sightings. Bring a telephoto lens for bird photography. The ornithologist guide is a significant enhancement to the birding experience — confirm availability with the lodge. Lake Nakuru is also home to both white and black rhino, lion, and leopard within its fenced national park.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn game drive within Lake Nakuru National Park — explore the forested areas and open grasslands for rhino, lion, and the park's resident leopards often spotted in the yellow fever tree forests. The morning light on the lake with flamingos is exceptional for photography. Visit the Baboon Cliff viewpoint for a sweeping panoramic view of the entire lake and its pink flamingo shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Lake Nakuru to Samburu National Reserve (approximately 1.5 hours — via Nairobi or direct depending on availability). Check in to a luxury tented camp on the banks of the Ewaso Ng'iro River. Begin the Samburu Rare Species Game Drive — discover Kenya's exclusive 'Samburu Special Five': the reticulated giraffe, Grevy's zebra, Beisa oryx, Somali ostrich, and gerenuk. These species are found almost nowhere else in Kenya.
day_by_day.evening: Riverside sundowner on the banks of the Ewaso Ng'iro River — watch elephants, crocodiles, and hippos at the water's edge as the sun sets over the arid Samburu landscape. Return to camp for a traditional Samburu-inspired dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge before charter departure — eggs to order, fresh fruits, Kenyan teas, and pastries
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box for the charter transfer; light refreshments upon arrival at Samburu camp
meals.dinner: Samburu-inspired bush dinner at the luxury tented camp — camel milk soup, spiced goat skewers with Samburu herbs, saffron-scented rice, and a date and honey dessert, served around a traditional campfire with Kenyan craft beers and wines

day_by_day.notes: Samburu is one of Kenya's most remote and authentic wilderness areas — the landscape and wildlife feel distinctly different from the Mara and Amboseli. The Ewaso Ng'iro River is a lifeline for wildlife and provides extraordinary game viewing directly from the camp. Samburu warriors may be present at the camp as cultural ambassadors — a wonderful opportunity for cultural exchange.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in Samburu National Reserve — the golden morning light on the arid landscape and the Samburu Special Five make for a spectacular farewell to the Kenyan wilderness. Spend time at the river watching elephants cross and crocodiles bask. Return to camp for a leisurely final breakfast in the bush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Samburu back to Nairobi (approximately 1 hour). Transfer to a luxury hotel in Nairobi for a final afternoon of leisure — consider visiting the Giraffe Centre to hand-feed endangered Rothschild giraffes, or the David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage for a farewell encounter with baby elephants (if timing allows). Final luxury shopping at a curated Nairobi boutique for premium Kenyan crafts, jewellery, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Nairobi's finest restaurants — a celebratory final meal reflecting on an extraordinary 10-day Kenyan journey. Private transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for onward departure.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell bush breakfast at Samburu luxury camp — full cooked breakfast with champagne toast, fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan speciality coffees, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Nairobi restaurant or hotel — light and elegant meal with Kenyan fusion cuisine
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Nairobi's top fine dining restaurant (e.g., Talisman or Carnivore for a classic Kenyan experience) — premium multi-course meal with Kenyan game meats, local produce, and an exceptional wine list, celebrating the conclusion of a world-class safari journey

day_by_day.notes: Confirm charter flight timings carefully to allow sufficient time for international check-in (minimum 3 hours before departure recommended). Duty-free Kenyan coffee, tea, and crafts make excellent last-minute purchases at the airport. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs purchased comply with CITES regulations — reputable retailers will confirm compliance. A gratuity for guides, trackers, and camp staff is customary and deeply appreciated — your concierge can advise on appropriate amounts.
